newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation on PaineWebber holds.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation on PaineWebber holds.

text.p: Speculation that brokerage PaineWebber Group Inc will be bought out remained solid Wednesday despite the surprise merger of two industry stalwarts, Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter, Discover & Co, traders said.
Traders said PaineWebber shares had been trending higher over the last couple of weeks on growing talk the company was set to be taken over.
But after reaching a new 52-week high at 39 Tuesday, the stock was down 3-1/4 at 35-5/8 at 1215 CST/1815 GMT Wednesday. The stock was the only major brokerage stock to decline.
"There is more options volume in PaineWebber than in Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter combined," said Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
He said some of that volume could be from investors disappointed that PaineWebber was not involved in a deal.
Bill Gorman at Lakota trading in Chicago said retail and institutional buying of PaineWebber call options had risen dramatically in the last couple of weeks as the stock rose.
"What's happened today, even with the stock down, there are still a lot of call buyers out there," he said. "More than call sellers."

He said some investors, still betting on the chance that PaineWebber will be involved in some kind of deal, used the decline in the stock, which drove call prices down, to pick up calls at lower prices.
The most active PaineWebber call was the February 40, which traded about 975 contracts. The option was down 7/8 at 7/8. Its open interest was 1,318, with 1,168 contracts added on Tuesday.
The February 35 call traded about 885 contracts. It lost 2-1/8 to 2-3/8. Other busy PaineWebber calls included the March 40s, the April 40s and the July 40s.
Options on both Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter were thinly traded Wednesday.
The most active Morgan Stanley option was the February 65 call, with volume of about 1,450. The option, which had open interest of 70 contracts, rose 1-1/4 to 1-3/8.
For Dean Witter, the busiest option was the March 40 call, which traded a total of about 866 contracts.
Most of that volume crossed on the Chicago Board Options Exchange, where the option was up 1/-1/16 at 2-3/16. Its open interest was 288 contracts.
The February 40 call and put were relatively busy.
"By the lack of option volume and the lack of volume preceding (the merger announcement), it looks like it took Wall Street by surprise," Schwartz said.

He added that there was very little options activity in the other major brokerage firms that are publicly traded, suggesting few investors expected a counter offer for either Dean Witter or Morgan Stanley to emerge.

"The stocks are up, but there's no options speculation that there could be a tender war or another candidate," he said, referring to the other brokerages. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750//Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
